title: Gold's Role in an AI-Driven Economy: Direct and Indirect Effects
gist: The World Gold Council argues gold's direct AI link (chip/data-centre usage; tech demand 323t in 2025, ~6-7% of demand) is small, and that AI matters for gold mainly through four indirect channels: energy-driven inflation and geopolitics/uncertainty (supportive) versus productivity-driven higher real rates and AI-enhanced mining supply (headwinds). The net sign is uncertain and time-varying, as shown by the sharp post-midterm repricing of AI equities.

themes.theme: Direct AI demand for gold is small

insights.claim: Gold has a direct but small link to AI: it is used in high-end chips, memory, connectors and networking equipment in AI data centres because few materials match its conductivity and corrosion resistance.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite a gold bull case on AI hardware demand; the physical use case is real but marginal.
insights.quote: The direct link between gold and AI is real but small in the context of the overall market.
insights.locator: The direct link between gold and AI

insights.claim: Technology demand for gold totalled 323 tonnes in 2025, virtually unchanged from 2024, and represents only around 6-7% of annual gold demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Tech fabrication is too small a slice of demand to singlehandedly move the gold price.
insights.quote: Technology demand for gold totalled 323 tonnes in 2025, virtually unchanged from 2024
insights.locator: The direct link between gold and AI

insights.claim: Gold use in electronics is a 'tug-of-war': AI demand pulls usage higher while high gold prices push manufacturers to thin out or substitute gold wherever possible.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: High gold prices self-limit industrial demand via thrifting and substitution, capping AI-driven fabrication upside.
insights.quote: AI demand is pulling gold usage higher, while high prices are pushing manufacturers to thin out or replace gold wherever they can.

insights.claim: The World Gold Council argues AI's indirect effects on energy costs, inflation, real rates and geopolitics will matter far more for gold than direct industrial demand, because they feed the actual drivers of the gold price.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Analyse AI's gold impact through macro drivers (rates, inflation, uncertainty), not through chip fabrication tonnage.
insights.quote: But AI’s indirect effects on energy costs, inflation, real rates and geopolitics I believe will carry far more weight for the gold market
insights.locator: In my recent conversations with investors

insights.claim: AI has become a major source of US growth, with a handful of companies driving much of the expansion in recent years, making it a dominant question in investor conversations about gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Concentrated AI-led growth makes the US macro path, and thus gold drivers, sensitive to a few companies' capex.
insights.locator: In my recent conversations with investors

insights.claim: Four channels link AI to gold: energy and inflation (supportive), productivity and real rates (headwind), uncertainty and geopolitics (supportive), and AI in mining and supply (modest headwind).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Use the four-channel map as a checklist to judge whether AI news is net bullish or bearish for gold.
insights.quote: Energy and inflation, uncertainty and geopolitics can be supportive, while productivity, real rates and changes in mining and supply can work against them.
insights.locator: These forces are not all moving in the same direction

insights.claim: The AI buildout's massive power and infrastructure needs are inflationary in the near term, as higher electricity costs feed consumer prices and heavy capex competes for economy-wide resources, which historically supports gold as an inflation hedge.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising power prices from data-centre demand are a near-term tailwind for gold's inflation-hedge bid.
insights.quote: The AI buildout requires enormous amounts of power and physical infrastructure, and that demand is inflationary in the near term.
insights.locator: The first is energy and inflation

insights.claim: If AI delivers productivity gains, faster growth with lower unit labour costs could ease inflation and push real interest rates higher, creating a headwind for gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A visible AI productivity boom would be a bearish gold signal via higher real rates; watch real yields.
insights.quote: Real interest rates would likely rise in that scenario, creating a headwind for gold.
insights.locator: The second is the impact of AI

insights.claim: AI's net effect on gold is time-varying and hard to call: it looks inflationary today but may prove disinflationary later, so which force dominates at any moment is very uncertain.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Expect the sign of AI's influence on gold to flip over time; avoid static AI-gold trade theses.
insights.quote: AI looks inflationary today and may prove disinflationary later.
insights.locator: These forces are not all moving in the same direction

insights.claim: Export controls and US-China competition over advanced chips have made AI adoption a political question, adding to uncertainty that historically draws central banks and households toward gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Escalation in chip export controls is a potential catalyst for safe-haven and reserve gold demand.
insights.quote: Whether economies embrace AI or not is now a political question as well as a technological one.
insights.locator: The third is uncertainty and geopolitics

insights.claim: AI-related uncertainty strengthens the case for central banks to diversify reserves into gold as a neutral asset with no counterparty risk, reinforcing a trend already in place before AI.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Central bank purchases remain a structural pillar; AI-era uncertainty adds to, rather than creates, that bid.
insights.quote: a neutral asset with no counterparty risk, a trend that was firmly in place before AI entered the picture
insights.locator: The third is uncertainty and geopolitics

insights.claim: For households, especially in emerging markets, AI raises questions about the future of work and savings, triggering a wealth-preservation instinct that gold has long served.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: AI-driven job anxiety could add to retail gold demand in emerging markets.
insights.quote: This uncertainty results in an instinct to preserve wealth; a role gold has long filled for many.
insights.locator: The third is uncertainty and geopolitics

insights.claim: Miners already apply AI to exploration targeting, ore-body modelling, predictive maintenance and autonomous operation, which over time could lower costs and modestly lift gold supply.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: AI may compress miner costs, but supply response is slow; a modest, long-dated headwind for gold price.
insights.quote: Over time, AI-driven advancements could lower costs and modestly lift future supply.

insights.claim: Geology, permitting and capital intensity will continue to constrain new gold supply regardless of AI advances, limiting AI's supply-side impact to a modest headwind.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Do not expect AI to unlock a supply glut; mine supply remains structurally constrained.
insights.quote: Still, geology, permitting and capital intensity will continue to constrain how much new gold reaches the market

insights.claim: After the 2026 US midterm elections, AI-linked equities sharply repriced as divided government, local voter-approved restrictions on new data centre development in dozens of jurisdictions, and doubts about AI spending's growth payoff hit sentiment.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Local data-centre restrictions are a new political risk for AI capex and can move markets quickly.
insights.quote: Voters in dozens of local jurisdictions approved restrictions on new data centre development, and markets questioned whether AI spending can deliver the growth it promises.
insights.locator: What we can say is that these effects

insights.claim: Tighter AI regulation will likely create a supportive backdrop for gold, though the signals are still developing.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Track AI regulatory tightening as an emerging gold-supportive signal.
insights.quote: The advancement of tighter AI regulations will likely create a supportive backdrop for gold, but the signals are still developing.
insights.locator: What we can say is that these effects

insights.claim: The key gold-market signals remain unchanged — real yields, the US dollar, investment flows and central bank purchases — but AI will change how they move and how often the market must rethink its assumptions.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Keep the standard gold dashboard but expect more frequent regime shifts and higher volatility in its drivers due to AI.
insights.quote: What AI will change is how those signals move, and most critically how often the market will need to rethink its assumptions.
